payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery chemistry designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. An independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit corrected the prototype’s cycle-life claim to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle figure because it used an un-normalized depth of discharge. The battery’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. Its projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Operation must be suspended below an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.
